props.title: Emily Barnes
props.face: Covers and originals, solo, as a duo or as a trio.
props.lede: Some singers fill the background, and some make everyone go quiet and lean in. Emily Barnes is the second kind. She’s an award-winning folk singer-songwriter who plays Joni Mitchell, Fleetwood Mac and Dolly Parton alongside her own songs, and she can play on her own for a ceremony or a dinner, or bring guitar, fiddle and harmonies as a duo or a trio.
props.headingNote: Here’s how booking through Signet works.

props.title: Emily Barnes playing her song Say It Again live at The Black Rose Acoustic Society

props.html: Emily won the 2025 Hey Nonny Songwriting Contest, and in 2026 the Colorado Music Business Organization named her one of the ten winners of its songwriting contest. She’s been a finalist at the Kerrville Folk Festival’s New Folk competition, the Red Lodge Songwriting Festival and The Acorn Songwriting Contest, too. Critics have compared her to Brandi Carlile and Joan Baez.

She grew up in Johnsonburg, New Jersey, a town of under a hundred people, writing songs on the stone steps of her family’s 200-year-old house. She’s made four albums since, and her album Mint Condition took her on a sold-out tour of the Northeast. These days she plays all over Colorado, from Denver and Boulder to Fort Collins and Grand Junction.

Last year she played 165 shows of her own music and 45 private events, so she knows how to hold a listening crowd and how to keep a cocktail hour easy and warm. She brings her own sound system, and she’s happy to plan the night around the songs you love.

props.title: Configurations
props.note: Send us your date and we’ll help you choose the size that works best. She can change up the players to fit the style or theme of your event, too.

rows.text: Book her solo for your ceremony, then bring in the duo or the trio for your cocktail hour and dinner. Landslide and You’ve Got a Friend are hard to beat for a first dance.
She’s a great fit for a birthday, an anniversary or a dinner at home, when you want music people actually stop and listen to.
A Colorado songwriter telling the stories behind her songs makes a warm evening for a team or for clients after a long day of meetings.
The trio’s guitar, fiddle and harmonies give a party a full sound without drums, so your guests can still talk.

props.html: Planning toasts or a program? We can work the music around them with your run of show. You can also get a general idea of what live music costs in Colorado from our cost guide.

items.q: Does she play covers or her own songs?
items.a: She plays both. Her song list runs from Joni Mitchell and Carole King to Fleetwood Mac, Brandi Carlile and Coldplay, and she’s happy to mix in her own songs. We’ll work out the balance with you.

items.q: Can she keep the volume down during dinner?
items.a: Yes. Solo or as a duo, she plays at a level where your guests can talk easily, and the trio has no drums.

items.q: Does she bring her own sound?
items.a: Yes, she brings her own sound system. Just let us know how big the space is and whether you’re indoors or out.

items.q: Does she play in the mountains?
items.a: Yes. She plays all over Colorado and often stays in Summit County, so Breckenridge, Vail and other mountain weddings and retreats are an easy fit. Tell us where your event is and we’ll let you know what’s possible.
